title: fix(pm): label-write --land reads the dogfood report on every card a fold's equal Fixes lines deliver
body:

_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuHka1976wP4xy6h8NTgreuq)_
Fixes #35651
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感：这是车队内部的落地工具；改动后，合并成一个拉取请求的多张卡，每张都写"修复"也能走自动落地，不必再把其中一张手工降级。
- 为什么做：落实"共享同一文件或机制的卡默认合并成一个拉取请求"这条常设指令，去掉每次合并都要手工关卡的那一步。
- 出错会怎样：只影响席位落地带破坏性标记的合并拉取请求时的那道冒烟测试检查；出错时它照旧拒绝、不写任何东西，直接撤回本拉取请求即可恢复原行为。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

`label-write.mjs --land` runs a dogfood-battery gate on a breaking or narrowing pull. It asked `deliveredCardNumber` for the ONE card thread holding the `os-dev-report`; a folded pull carries one `Fixes` line per card at equal strength, `deliveredCardNumber` reports that tie (`card: null`) instead of breaking it, and the gate refused with "no card". The workaround was demoting a line to `Part of` and closing that card by hand.

This takes the seat's Route B and leaves the record pairing alone:

- `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`: a new exported sibling, `deliveredCardsAtStrongest(pr)`, returns every delivered card at the strongest grade, in body order, with that grade. It and `deliveredCardNumber` both answer from one private enumeration (`strongestDeliveredRows`), which asks `deliveryEvidence` exactly as before, so there is no second parser. `deliveredCardNumber`'s answers are unchanged, the tie included, so the queue guard's and `check-owed-reviews.mjs`'s pairing behaves byte-identically. Its docblock rule ("AMBIGUITY IS NOT RESOLVED, it is REPORTED") still holds: nothing picks a card by number order.
- `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs` `landDogfoodGate`: on a tie it reads EVERY tied card's thread in full, with the same page cap, the same trusted-author filter and the same sibling-pull rule as the single-card path. It lands when the head, or one shared first-parent walk from it, reaches ANY tied card's battery sha. The verdict cannot depend on reading order. A tie refusal names every tied card read and why each failed (`landDogfoodRefusal` prints `reports: card #A …; card #B …`). A tied thread that does not read is still exit 3 (`unread: true`), and one that cannot be read whole still refuses, whatever the other cards carry. A body naming no card still refuses as before. The single-card path keeps its reads and messages: all 50 pre-existing cases in that battery pass unchanged.
- The `--land` pass line on a tie adds ` · a tie of N cards (#A, #B), every thread read, cleared by card #A comment X`.

Not touched: `.claude/**` (no tie-break line was added, so the card's third Done-when bullet, `execution-duties.md`'s fold text, does not apply), `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`, `check-owed-reviews.mjs`.

Branch note for the Duplicate Fix Guard: `claude/project-thread-fatvim` is the platform-fixed branch of this card thread, the only branch this container can push. It is not issue-numbered, and the card is #35651.

### Read first (by risk)

1. `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs` `landDogfoodGate`: the `readCard` / `outcomes` / `pass` / `walkRefuse` hunk. Risk: the single-card path must stay unchanged in reads and in text.
2. `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` `strongestDeliveredRows` / `deliveredCardNumber`: the refactor must leave `deliveredCardNumber`'s answers exactly as they were.
3. `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs` `landDogfoodRefusal` and the `② dogfood gate ✓` line: the printed shape on a tie.

### Two-minute verification

`node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs --self-test`: expect `✓ label-write self-test: 334 cases pass across 18 batteries`, with the case `⭐ PASSES: a ! fold whose body carries TWO Fixes lines and a dogfood report on the chain-head card` among them.

## Tests

Final head ``c398e4802``.

- `label-write.mjs --self-test`: the dogfood-gate battery floor goes from 50 to 65, with 15 new cases. Passing cases: two `Fixes` with the report on the chain-head card; the same with the lines swapped (order-independence, threads read in body order #9 then #8); the report on the second-named card; a `Part of` tie; a tied card's battery one merge of main below the head, over an `n/a` on the other card; the sibling-pull rule applied per card. Refusing cases: no tied card carries a report (it names both cards and why each failed); `n/a` on one card and a non-merge walk on the other; a shared walk refused on a non-base merge; the walk naming each distinct battery sha once; an untrusted report on a tied card. NOT MEASURED cases (exit 3): an unread tied thread, even with the other card clearing, and an unread walk commit on a tie. One case for a tied thread answering no list. One structural pin: the gate reads a tie only through `deliveredCardsAtStrongest(pull.json)`, enumerates nothing itself, and ranks nothing (`sort`, `Math.min`/`Math.max` absent).
- `record-recognisers.mjs --self-test`: one new battery (8 cases), and the roster floor goes from 19 to 20. Its cases: a two-keyword tie in body order and never sorted; `deliveredCardNumber` still `card: null` on that body; a `Part of` tie; a stronger grade leaves one card; a branch adds nothing once the body speaks; no card gives an empty result; a control that one card in the tie equals `deliveredCardNumber`'s card on every fixture, and none equals its null; a structural pin that both relations call `strongestDeliveredRows(pr)` and neither calls `deliveryEvidence(` directly.
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test` passes unedited. Its existing case `⛔ and-a-pull-request-delivering-TWO-cards-at-equal-strength-picks-NEITHER` already pins the pairing unchanged on a tie: it refuses and reads only the PR thread.

```

node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --self-test          EXIT=0  ✓ record-recognisers self-test: 459 cases pass
node scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test  EXIT=0  ✓ check-governed-queue-guard self-test: 581 cases pass
node scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs --self-test          EXIT=0  ✓ check-owed-reviews self-test: 94 cases pass in 10 batteries
```

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation: the gate hunk reverted to origin/main, with the fix committed</summary>

Done with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor was the new gate body, from `const delivered = deliveredCardNumber(pull.json);` to the end of the function, and the replacement was the same region at `598a34d04`. Then `node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs --self-test` ran.

```
ablation-replace:   anchor hits 1 time(s), as declared
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob eabe0e5d1a57 -> 550b388c54c3
  ✗ ⭐ PASSES: a `!` fold whose body carries TWO `Fixes` lines and a dogfood report on the chain-head card — exit 0, ready and armed, both threads read — … why: no card: it delivers 2 cards at the same strength (#8, #9, via a closing keyword) …
  ✗ …the verdict does not follow number or body order: …
  ✗ …and a report on the SECOND-named card clears it the same way — …
✗ label-write self-test: 15 of 334 case(s) failed.
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (eabe0e5d1a57) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

All 15 new cases went red on the old gate: every fold refuses with "no card". The 319 earlier cases stayed green. The restore was proven by blob hash equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Route B was taken, as the seat preferred: the fix is confined to the gate plus an additive sibling relation. `deliveredCardNumber` and its readers (`check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` ×3, `check-owed-reviews.mjs`) are byte-identical in behaviour, so no rule text changes and this PR stays off the governed register.
- On H2 (the branch name as a chain-head signal): not relied on. Once a body declares a card, `deliveryEvidence` already rejects the branch-name grade, and the fold PR that hit this defect carried an issue-numbered branch, while card threads push `claude/project-thread-*`.
- A tie costs N thread listings, one per tied card, and at most one shared commit walk, not one per card.
- The `record-recognisers.mjs` header names the new export on `deliveredCardNumber`'s own line. Adding a header line would move the `dispatch-gates: self-test-reads` declaration off line 77, which `dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` pins in its census. The first local run of `check:pm-dispatch-gates` went red on exactly that, and this PR's third commit fixed it.
- Overlap: PR #35610 (draft) shares `record-recognisers.mjs`. `overlap-check.mjs` was run before every push: `VERDICT clean exit 0`, merging cleanly. The new battery's roster row and floor bump sit outside #35610's hunks.

## Verification

Local subset at `c398e4802`, with each exit code captured before any pipe: the 64 families `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives for this diff (2 paths).

- 63 exit 0. This includes `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` (`✓ dispatch-gates self-test (fast tier): 2249 cases pass`), `pnpm check:pm-label-write`, `pnpm check:pm-record-recognisers`, `node scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test`, `pnpm check:nul-bytes` and `pnpm check:issue-citations`.
- 1 NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET. It needs the built workspace closure (`dist/`), this diff touches no package, and it is left to CI.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran ran.list`: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 64 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 63 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED`.
- `node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs --branch=claude/project-thread-fatvim`: `VERDICT clean exit 0` before each push.
- No changeset: `scripts/pm/**` publishes nothing, so this PR carries `skip-changeset`. No `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm, so the dogfood battery is n/a.
- Every other family (lint, typecheck, Test Core, the governed queue guard) is CI's, read from this PR's check-runs.
